title: Overthinking, Rumination & Mental Loops
description: Explore planning versus looping through dialogue, evidence and psychological reasoning.

lessons.title: Preparation that stops preparing you
lessons.teach: Follow the conversation one message at a time. Notice what the behaviour might be achieving before you decide why it happened. About five minutes.
lessons.objective: Distinguish observable evidence from a tentative explanation of planning versus looping.

nodes.title: What might be happening?
nodes.body:
Effective planning reduces uncertainty by producing a decision or test. Repetitive worry can feel productive even when it yields no new evidence. Rewriting may briefly soothe Rae's fear of being caught out while delaying the spoken rehearsal that would actually test the answer.

Further preparation is rational when there is a genuine knowledge gap. The difference is whether the next round of thinking can change a decision or action.
nodes.sources: Watkins (2008), Constructive and Unconstructive Repetitive Thought.

lessons.title: What would change your mind?
lessons.teach: An initial explanation is useful only if it can be challenged. Revisit the characters, test a rival account and apply the idea in another setting. About five minutes.
lessons.objective: Test an account of planning versus looping with new evidence and transfer it to a new case.

nodes.title: One distinction to keep
nodes.prompt: Fill the missing word: An explanation of what a behaviour might achieve is a working ______, not a proven fact.
nodes.explanation: A hypothesis is an explanation that can be revised when observations fail to support it. This keeps psychological reasoning useful rather than turning it into confident mind-reading.
